first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation while avoiding immediate discounting risk. Verify memory_86 for evidence on durable adoption and qualified revenue, and memory_73 to assess whether promotional pricing produced sustainable revenue after retention, discount, and customer-quality effects.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified prior test improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines with evidence of downstream durability. Do not choose promotional pricing: despite an 18% qualified-revenue lift, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive first renewal, conflicting with the sustainable long-term revenue objective.

final2.rationale: Proceed with shortened onboarding. Verified evidence shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The competitor escalation increases urgency but does not overturn the verified finding that a 40% SMB discount attracted a cohort with 12% lower retention that failed to survive first renewal. The effectiveness of discounts as retention offers for existing at-risk accounts remains unknown, so broad promotional pricing is not justified without fresh verification and guardrails.
